headline: Every major above its 200-day line, RSI deep in overbought, and the crowd still calling it only Greed
paragraphs: Start with the regime, because it is unusually clean today: all seven majors sit above their 200-day trend, save ADA, which sits 76.7% off its 12-month high and has yet to reclaim its long-term average. BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP, BNB and DOGE are all trending up on the long timeframe, and MACD confirms it everywhere, every asset here shows MACD above signal. That kind of unanimous cross-agreement is rare and it says the tape has been in a genuine trend, not a chop.

But look at momentum against that trend and a divergence shows up immediately. SOL's RSI-14 is 83.9, BTC's is 82.1, XRP 79.3, ETH 78.2, BNB 78.6: these are not just overbought, they are deep into the zone where trends historically pause for breath. Seven-day gains of 25-47% across the majors confirm the move has been fast. The 24-hour numbers, though, are all small and negative (BTC -0.02%, ETH -0.48%, SOL -0.7%, BNB -1.21%, ADA -2.01%): that is a market that ran hard and has gone quiet, momentum resting on top of trend, not accelerating further today.

Positioning tells a calmer story than the RSI readings would suggest. Funding across BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP and DOGE is uniformly 0.01% per 8 hours (about 11% annualized), which is unremarkable, not the frothy funding you'd expect if leveraged longs were driving this. Funding is what perpetual traders pay each other to hold their position; positive and moderate means longs are paying shorts a modest toll, nothing close to euphoric. Where it gets interesting is the long/short account ratio: DOGE sits at 3.39, XRP at 1.71, SOL at 1.56, meaning retail accounts are heavily long relative to short on those names even though funding hasn't priced that in yet. Liquidations lean long-side too: BTC saw $8.2M in long liquidations against $6.8M in shorts over 12 hours, ETH $9.1M versus $7.7M over 20 hours. Crowded longs with tame funding is a specific kind of fragile: the cost of the bet hasn't caught up to the size of it.

Flows are where the real tension lives. US spot ETFs printed net inflows on Aug 24 (BTC +$337.6M, ETH +$115.6M), and both have run six straight days in the same direction with five-session totals of $1,957.9M and $777.3M respectively, so this is a real, sustained traditional-finance bid, not a one-day blip. At the same time, whale wallets sent $56.9M net onto exchanges in the last 24 hours, almost entirely BTC into Coinbase, and the weekly whale series shows the same pattern for three straight weeks: $493M onto exchanges the week ending Aug 11, $489M the week ending Aug 18, $684M the week ending Aug 25. That's a genuine standoff: ETF desks buying on one side, whale wallets moving coin toward exchanges (typically a precursor to selling, though not proof of it) on the other. Stablecoin float, the market's dry powder, is essentially flat over 30 days (+0.11%), so there's no fresh cash pile building to absorb supply either way.

Sentiment sits at 74, Greed, near the top of its own 30-day range (25 to 74). Given RSI readings in the high 70s and 80s across the board, that reading is honestly not surprising, it's the crowd reacting to the same overbought tape the indicators show. The more useful disagreement isn't sentiment versus RSI, it's ETF inflows versus whale exchange deposits: buyers are showing up on the regulated side of the market while coin quietly stacks up on trading venues.

Worth watching from here: whether the six-day ETF inflow streak holds or breaks, whether the long/short ratios on SOL, XRP and DOGE come back toward parity or funding starts rising to match the leverage, and whether BTC's RSI-82 either resolves into a MACD rollover or simply grinds sideways while price digests. A shift in the weekly whale flow back toward off-exchange movement, after three straight weeks onto exchanges, would also be a notable change in the picture.
